hypotheses.confidence_note: Trusted inputs are acquisition times, calibrations, ego history and configured dynamics; all environmental metres are conditional estimates. Metric grounding uses calibrated viewing directions, hypothesized approximately level pavement and visible foot/tyre contacts, with pedestrian and van size priors. Curb and barrier locations support only a local convex road patch before the leftward junction; the patch does not include the construction enclosure. This is not a verified ground-plane reconstruction or measured triangulation. History and supplied ego poses support a lead van continuing left; its instantaneous speed is not reliably separated from ego motion. The van envelope deliberately bounds the entire adopted five-second body sweep, including stopping and forward/left continuation up to roughly 6 m/s, using an approximately 5 by 2 m body. Worker envelopes cover standing and walking off the island toward the crossing, with longitudinal wandering and approximately 1.2 m/s lateral walking. The striped pedestrian at the left curb may wait, walk along the curb or enter the road at walking speed up to approximately 1.5 m/s. Each repeated polygon is an intentionally coarse whole-horizon body-and-motion envelope, hence also covers each exact subinterval; it is not a repeated stationary-body prediction. Coordinate uncertainties separately allow for contact, scale and alignment errors. Recent side frames differ by at most 43 ms; actor movement during those offsets is absorbed in residual uncertainty, not treated as time-aligned by ego compensation alone. Earlier front images are used for qualitative motion rather than unchanged actor positions. The right-crossing group and junction vehicles are visibly relevant, but individual associations, approach speeds and potential entrances behind barriers cannot be bounded credibly here; their occupancy remains null. The unknown polygon locates the concern and is not an asserted intrusion bound, so unbounded_unknown remains true. Visible green signals face other junction movements and do not establish ego permission; the give-way sign applies to this approach. The requested stop is precautionary, not an asserted mandatory stop-sign rule. At 4.98 m/s, maximum braking needs about 1.66 s and 4.14 m; a 2.1 s stop within 5.5 m is dynamically plausible before additional steering and collision checks. The ego is already at the zebra crossing, so this does not claim a stop before that crossing. Pedestrian envelopes may conflict with even the stopping maneuver, and unresolved traffic prevents a verified permission to proceed. No downstream feasibility or grounding verification has been performed.
